description:
FILED s470bl (Opus, 2026-09-05), probed vs perl 5.40.3 while shipping #1022
half (b).  PCL is MORE PERMISSIVE than perl here, which is the least harmful
direction, and the shape occurs in no corpus.

    sub f { last }
    my $n = 0;
    for my $i (1..3) { $n++; my @x = sort { f(); $a <=> $b } (3,1,2); $n += 100 }
      perl:  Can't "last" outside a loop block
      PCL:   n=1     (the loop is exited)

    sub f { last }                       # the map spelling, for contrast
    for my $i (1..3) { $n++; my @y = map { f(); $_ } (1,2); $n += 100 }
      perl:  n=1     PCL: n=1            -- a map block IS transparent

    grep: same as map (probed, n=1 both).

perl's sort comparator is a pseudo-frame it will not `last` out of; its map and
grep blocks are not.  PCL has no such boundary: the throw reaches the
enclosing loop's frame.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: bind *p-dyn-loop-frames* to 0 around the SORT CALL (not
per comparison) inside p-sort, which is one special bind per `sort` -- cheap,
but it is a bind on a hot path the bench measures (sortnum/sortstr do 20k
sorts), so measure before shipping.  Also decide whether the same boundary
belongs on a `sort SUBNAME`/`sort $cmp` call.

=== DONE (s473e, Opus, 2026-09-08) ===
SHIPPED, exactly as the task said it would close: `p-sort` binds
`*p-dyn-loop-frames*` to 0 for its CALL, so `%p-dyn-loop-exit` reads zero and
takes perl's own `Can't "last" outside a loop block` at the exit's own site
instead of throwing past the sort.

THE THREE COMPARATOR SPELLINGS ARE ALL BOUNDARIES (probed vs perl 5.40.3, which
the task left open): block, `sort SUBNAME` and `sort $cmp` all die.  So one bind
in `p-sort` covers all three -- every comparator form resolves through it.
`map`/`grep` stay transparent in both languages.  `%p-sort-classic` needs no
bind: its licence is plain scalars and builtin comparators, and every other case
it hands back to `p-sort`.  The bind also covers the list collection, where a
tie FETCH or an overload handler could run user code -- perl refuses a `last`
from those too.

COST, the measurement the task asked for: a RUNTIME A/B (`BENCH_RT_B` against a
92d2eb74 runtime -- one shared transpile, interleaved, so the two columns differ
by exactly the runtime; `bench-emission-ab.pl` is the wrong instrument here, it
A/Bs EMISSIONS and this change emits nothing).  Five runs at K=5..9 on a box at
load ~8: `sortnum` reads -1.2 % .. +1.2 % and `sortstr` -2.1 % .. +0.8 %, while
the byte-identical `intloop` CONTROL rows on the SAME runs read -4.1 % .. +0.2 %.
Inside the instrument's own noise, and bounded above arithmetically at ~0.2 %
(20 000 special binds against a 111 ms row).  Well under the 2 % bar.

Guard `Pl/t/loop-exit-01.t` section 12 (6 rows, 2 of them the inverses).  The
`sort $cmp` row carries a deliberate `g(0)` call: without it that loop takes no
frame at all and the row would pass on both trees for the WRONG reason.
docs/ir-spec.md 6.2 and docs/not-supported.md updated.
subject: A `sort` COMPARATOR is a `last` boundary in perl and is not one in PCL: `for (â¦) { sort { f() } â¦ }` with `sub f { last }` dies in perl and exits the loop in PCL (map/grep blocks are transparent in BOTH)
